Dallas County centers on Selma, the Black Belt's historic capital on the Alabama River and site of the Edmund Pettus Bridge. The county carries civil-rights tourism, catfish and row-crop agriculture, and a housing stock of significant antebellum and Victorian architecture priced well below state averages.
Source: U.S. Census Bureau · Data verified: October 26, 2026
